children: Thanksgiving

shopping is no longer just about who offers the deepest discounts. Increasingly, it is about who makes buying something easiest when consumers are away from their computers. That shift could create an opportunity for
Apple Inc.
Amazon.com, Inc.
and digital payment companies as
become an increasingly important part of America’s biggest shopping season.
Smartphones Are Becoming Shopping Malls

Adobe expects Americans to spend $4.4 billion shopping on mobile devices on Thanksgiving Day 2026, an 11% increase from 2025. Even more telling, mobile devices are forecast to account for 63% of Thanksgiving’s online sales, up from 61.6% last year, according to Adobe’s holiday shopping forecast.

The broader opportunity is significant. Adobe expects total Thanksgiving online spending to reach $6.9 billion, up 8.5% year over year. That means mobile shopping is no longer a secondary channel retailers can afford to overlook. It is becoming central to how consumers discover deals, compare prices and complete purchases.
For investors, the shift creates several potential beneficiaries across the shopping ecosystem, although not all of them capture spending in the same way.
Apple Owns the Device. Amazon Owns the Destination.
For Apple, the opportunity begins with the device itself. The
iPhone
is increasingly the shopping screen consumers carry everywhere, while
Apple Pay
makes completing purchases easier. Shoppers can use Face ID or Touch ID to authenticate payments in supported apps and websites without repeatedly entering card and shipping details.

However, investors should distinguish between a growing mobile shopping market and direct revenue gains for Apple. The company does not earn a percentage of every retail purchase simply because an iPhone user shops on the device. Its opportunity is broader: strengthening the value of its hardware and services ecosystem.

Amazon, meanwhile, has a more direct connection to the spending itself. Its shopping app lets consumers browse millions of products, compare prices, read reviews, receive deal notifications and track deliveries. Those features make it easier to turn a few minutes of browsing on a smartphone into an actual purchase. Amazon has continued adding shopping and discovery tools to its app, including AI-powered shopping guides and visual product discovery.
Payment Companies Want a Cut
The mobile shopping opportunity extends beyond retailers and device makers.
PayPal Holdings, Inc.
and
Shopify Inc.
provide infrastructure that helps merchants convert mobile browsing into completed transactions.

PayPal’s checkout offering gives merchants access to multiple payment options, including Venmo and Pay Later. That matters during the holiday rush, when a complicated payment process can give shoppers another reason to abandon their carts. PayPal’s checkout platform is designed to simplify that final step.

Shopify’s Shop Pay tackles the same challenge through saved payment and shipping details. The company says its accelerated checkout can deliver conversion rates up to 50% higher than standard checkout. Its checkout platform also supports one-tap payments across devices.
Investment Takeaway
Investors should watch whether rising mobile spending translates into stronger Amazon sales, higher merchant conversion rates and greater payment volumes for PayPal and Shopify.
The $4.4 billion forecast signals an opportunity, but execution will determine who captures the most value.
